title: Gospel
definition: The Gospel is the good news that God saves sinners by grace through the death, resurrection, and lordship of Jesus Christ.
summary: The Gospel is the good news that God saves sinners by grace through the death, resurrection, and lordship of Jesus Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Himself is the center of the Gospel: the crucified and risen Savior who brings sinners to God and gives new life by the Holy Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Gospel is not merely religious advice, moral improvement, or encouragement to try harder. It is the announcement of what God has done in Christ to save sinners who could not save themselves.

Scripture teaches that sin separates people from God and that Christ came to bear sin, conquer death, and call people to repentance and faith. The Gospel reveals both the seriousness of sin and the greater mercy of God.

The Gospel is the doorway into salvation and the foundation for daily discipleship. Believers never outgrow the good news; they learn to live from it, return to it, and proclaim it with humility and hope.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People carrying guilt, addiction, shame, spiritual confusion, or church wounds do not need a message that tells them to clean themselves up before coming to God. They need the good news that Christ came for sinners and makes dead people alive.

The Gospel keeps ministry centered. Without it, doctrine becomes cold, church becomes activity, and recovery becomes self-improvement instead of new life in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Return to the Gospel daily. Confess your need honestly, trust Christ’s finished work, reject performance-based acceptance, and ask the Holy Spirit to help you live as one who has been rescued by grace.
